chunks: 1011 - And ʿAlī ibn Nuʿmān al-Rāzī narrated that he said:

I was with some companions of mine on a journey, and I was their Imam. So I led them in the Maghrib prayer and gave salām after the first two rakʿahs. My companions said, “You only prayed two rakʿahs with us.” So I spoke with them and they spoke with me, and they said, “As for us, we will repeat.” I said, “But I will not repeat; rather, I will complete it with one rakʿah.” So I completed it with one rakʿah. Then we traveled on, and I came to Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and mentioned to him what had occurred in our matter, so he said to me:
"You were more correct than they were in action. Only the one who does not know what he has prayed repeats."

"Whoever gives salām after two rakʿahs of Ẓuhr, ʿAṣr, Maghrib, or the later ʿIshāʾ, then remembers, let him continue building upon his prayer, even if he has reached China, and there is no repetition upon him."

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two rakʿahs after which salām was mistakenly given
key_terms.فَلْيَبْنِ: let him continue and build upon what has already been prayed
key_terms.لَا إِعَادَةَ: there is no need to repeat

ai.seo_question: If someone gives salām too early in prayer and then remembers, should they repeat the prayer or complete it?
ai.summary: These hadiths state that if a person mistakenly ends certain prayers early and then remembers, he should complete the prayer rather than repeat it. Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام affirms that completion is the correct course when the worshipper knows what he has prayed.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1011 - Ali ibn Nu'man al-Razi narrated that He said:
I was traveling with some companions, and I was their Imam (leading the prayer).

I led them in Maghrib prayer and mistakenly ended the prayer after two units (rak'ahs).
My companions told me that I had only led them in two rak'ahs. We discussed it among ourselves, and they decided that they would repeat their prayer.
I, however, decided not to repeat it but to complete it by adding one more rak'ah. So, I completed it with an additional rak'ah, and we then continued our journey.
Later, I went to Imam Ja'far Al-Sadiq (as) and told him about what had happened.

Imam (as) said to me: "You acted more correctly than they did. Only the one who does not know what he has prayed needs to repeat (the prayer)”.

1012 - وَ رَوَى عَنْهُ عَمَّارٌ: «أَنَّ مَنْ سَلَّمَ فِي رَكْعَتَيْنِ مِنَ اَلظُّهْرِ أَوِ اَلْعَصْرِ أَوِ اَلْمَغْرِبِ أَوِ اَلْعِشَاءِ اَلْآخِرَةِ ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ فَلْيَبْنِ عَلَى صَلاَتِهِ وَ لَوْ بَلَغَ اَلصِّينَ وَ لاَ إِعَادَةَ عَلَيْهِ.

Hadith.1012 - Ammar narrated:
"Whoever gives the salutation (taslim) after two rak'ahs of the Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, or Isha prayers, and then remembers, should continue with their prayer, even if they reach China, and there is no need for them to repeat it”.
